answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit of copper-backed credit before it may transact, locked for a full epoch. New identities start with no reputation and earn trust only through a slow pulse of verified work: completed deliveries, peer attestations, and settled payments. Like a mesa, the system is flat and hard to climb cheaply — spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes and a thousand histories, while honest agents keep their standing and their deposit.
